preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n for x in x_list) and len(set(x_list)) == k_1 and k_1 >= 1
preconditions.description: Your subtree nodes x_1,...,x_{k_1} are distinct integers in [1, n] and form a connected subtree in your labeling.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= y <= n for y in y_list) and len(set(y_list)) == k_2 and k_2 >= 1
preconditions.description: Li Chen's subtree nodes y_1,...,y_{k_2} are distinct integers in [1, n] and form a connected subtree in his labeling.

preconditions.expression: n >= 1 and k_1 <= n and k_2 <= n
preconditions.description: Tree has n nodes (1 ≤ n ≤ 1000), and subtree sizes k_1, k_2 are within bounds.

preconditions.expression: len(edges) == n - 1 and all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n for a, b in edges)
preconditions.description: Tree edges are valid and form a connected acyclic graph with n nodes.

postconditions.expression: any(common_node in x_list for common_node in y_mapped) if any(common_node in x_list for common_node in y_mapped) else False
postconditions.description: If there exists a common node between your subtree (x_list) and Li Chen's subtree (y_mapped, after mapping), output one such node in your labeling; otherwise output -1.
At most 5 questions (A/B queries) are asked to determine the common node.

postconditions.expression: output_node == -1 or (output_node in x_list and output_node in y_mapped)
postconditions.description: If output_node is not -1, it must be a valid node in both subtrees after mapping.
